quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional accounting firm surveyed employees before and after introducing a policy that discouraged sending non-urgent emails after 6 p.m., encouraging staff to schedule messages for the next morning instead. Six months later, employees reported feeling less pressure to check their phones during evenings, and the firm's annual employee survey showed a modest but measurable increase in reported job satisfaction, particularly among employees with young children at home.
options: Job satisfaction declined most among employees with young children.
The policy had no measurable effect on employee satisfaction.
Employees reported feeling more pressure to check their phones after the policy began.
The email policy appears to have eased evening work pressure, especially for employees with children.
quests.correctAnswer: The email policy appears to have eased evening work pressure, especially for employees with children.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of employees showed the clearest change in satisfaction.
quests.explanation: Employees felt less evening pressure and satisfaction rose modestly overall, with the increase most notable among employees with young children, suggesting the policy specifically eased a burden that fell hardest on parents.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional water authority that had long struggled with algae blooms in a reservoir used for drinking water began requiring farms in the surrounding watershed to maintain vegetated buffer strips along streams feeding into the reservoir. Three years after the requirement took effect, water quality tests showed phosphorus levels in the reservoir had dropped by nearly a third, and algae blooms had become noticeably less frequent during summer months.
options: The buffer strip requirement appears to have improved the reservoir's water quality.
Phosphorus levels rose after the buffer strip requirement took effect.
Algae blooms became more frequent after the new requirement.
The buffer strips had no measurable effect on water quality.
quests.correctAnswer: The buffer strip requirement appears to have improved the reservoir's water quality.
quests.hint: Compare water quality measurements before and after the buffer strip requirement began.
quests.explanation: Phosphorus levels dropped and algae blooms became less frequent after farms began maintaining buffer strips, suggesting the vegetation was filtering runoff before it reached the reservoir.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional health system that once scheduled routine mammograms only during standard weekday business hours began offering a limited number of Saturday morning appointments at three of its clinics. Within the first year, the clinics offering weekend appointments saw screening rates rise among women in their forties, a group that had consistently shown the lowest screening compliance across the entire health system for the previous decade.
options: Screening rates among women in their forties fell after weekend appointments were added.
Weekend appointments had no measurable effect on screening rates for any age group.
Weekend appointments appear to have specifically helped raise screening rates among women in their forties.
Women in their forties had the highest screening compliance before the change.
quests.correctAnswer: Weekend appointments appear to have specifically helped raise screening rates among women in their forties.
quests.hint: Notice which specific age group's screening rate changed most after weekend hours were added.
quests.explanation: Screening rates rose specifically among women in their forties, the group with historically the lowest compliance, after weekend appointments became available, suggesting the new hours addressed a scheduling barrier that had particularly affected that age group.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team building a customer service chatbot found that when the bot was programmed to first acknowledge a customer's frustration in plain language before offering a solution, customer satisfaction ratings for those interactions were notably higher than ratings for interactions where the bot jumped straight to a solution, even when the solution offered to resolve the underlying issue was identical in both types of interactions, according to the team's internal review.
options: Acknowledging frustration before offering a solution appears to improve customer satisfaction.
Jumping straight to a solution led to higher satisfaction ratings.
The wording used by the chatbot had no bearing on satisfaction.
The solutions offered were different between the two types of interactions.
quests.correctAnswer: Acknowledging frustration before offering a solution appears to improve customer satisfaction.
quests.hint: Notice that the solution itself was identical; only the wording leading up to it changed.
quests.explanation: Interactions where the bot acknowledged frustration first received higher satisfaction ratings, even though the actual solution was the same, suggesting that how a response is framed matters as much as its content.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A district that had always assigned students to homerooms alphabetically by last name experimented with assigning a portion of incoming ninth graders to homerooms based on shared extracurricular interests instead, gathered from a survey students completed over the summer. Counselors later reported that students in interest-based homerooms were significantly more likely to say they had made a close friend within their first month of high school.
options: Grouping students by shared interests appears to have helped them form friendships more quickly.
Students in interest-based homerooms were less likely to report making friends.
Homeroom assignment method had no bearing on how quickly students made friends.
Alphabetical homerooms led to faster friendship formation than interest-based ones.
quests.correctAnswer: Grouping students by shared interests appears to have helped them form friendships more quickly.
quests.hint: Compare how quickly students made friends in each type of homeroom.
quests.explanation: Students grouped by shared interests reported making close friends faster than expected under the old alphabetical system, suggesting that starting with a shared interest gave students an easier way to connect early in high school.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A family counselor who works primarily with parents of teenagers observed that families who established a specific, predictable time each week for one-on-one activities between a parent and each individual child, separate from whole-family time, reported fewer instances of teenagers describing feeling 'unheard' in follow-up sessions conducted six months later, compared to families who relied only on spontaneous or whole-family interactions.
options: Scheduled one-on-one time increased how unheard teenagers felt.
Whole-family time alone was more effective than individual time.
Scheduled one-on-one time with a parent may reduce teenagers' sense of feeling unheard.
How families spent time together had no bearing on teenagers' sense of being heard.
quests.correctAnswer: Scheduled one-on-one time with a parent may reduce teenagers' sense of feeling unheard.
quests.hint: Compare the two approaches to family time and their effect on teenagers' feelings of being heard.
quests.explanation: Families with regular one-on-one time reported teenagers feeling less unheard than families relying only on group interactions, suggesting individual attention may address something whole-family time doesn't fully capture.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national park that had long relied on a first-come, first-served system for its most popular hiking permits switched to a lottery system requiring advance registration. Park rangers reported a notable decrease in the number of visitors who arrived at the trailhead only to be turned away, though early survey data suggested some spontaneous travelers who used to take their chances found the new system frustrating and less appealing.
options: The lottery system pleased every type of visitor equally.
More visitors were turned away after the lottery system began.
The lottery system had no effect on visitor experience of any kind.
The lottery system appears to have reduced turned-away visitors while creating a new frustration for spontaneous travelers.
quests.correctAnswer: The lottery system appears to have reduced turned-away visitors while creating a new frustration for spontaneous travelers.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes both a benefit and a new drawback of the lottery system.
quests.explanation: Fewer visitors were turned away under the lottery system, but some spontaneous travelers found it less appealing, suggesting the change traded one problem for a different kind of inconvenience rather than solving everything.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An analysis of small investors who used a robo-advisor platform that automatically rebalanced portfolios on a fixed schedule found that these investors were less likely to sell off assets during a period of market volatility than investors managing their own portfolios manually, even though both groups had access to identical investment information and market commentary throughout the downturn.
options: Investors managing portfolios manually were less likely to sell during volatility.
Automatic rebalancing may have helped investors avoid impulsive selling during volatile markets.
Access to information was the main factor determining selling behavior.
Both groups sold off assets at identical rates during the downturn.
quests.correctAnswer: Automatic rebalancing may have helped investors avoid impulsive selling during volatile markets.
quests.hint: Compare selling behavior between the two groups, noting that information access was equal.
quests.explanation: Investors using automatic rebalancing sold fewer assets during volatility than those managing portfolios manually, even with identical information available, suggesting the automated process itself may have reduced impulsive reactions to market swings.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A mid-sized city that had allowed street vendors to operate under a complex, multi-step permitting process simplified the system to a single annual fee and a one-page application. In the following year, the number of licensed street vendors more than doubled, and city officials noted a corresponding decline in reports of unlicensed vending in the areas where vendors had previously avoided the paperwork altogether.
options: The number of licensed vendors dropped after the process was simplified.
Unlicensed vending increased after the permitting process was simplified.
The complexity of the permitting process had no bearing on vendor licensing rates.
Simplifying the permit process appears to have encouraged more vendors to operate legally.
quests.correctAnswer: Simplifying the permit process appears to have encouraged more vendors to operate legally.
quests.hint: Compare licensed vendor numbers, and unlicensed vending reports, before and after the process was simplified.
quests.explanation: Licensed vendors more than doubled and unlicensed vending declined after the permit process became simpler, suggesting the earlier complexity had been discouraging vendors from seeking a license in the first place.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A high school athletic department that had always scheduled the same pre-season conditioning program for every sport, regardless of the specific physical demands of each sport, switched to sport-specific conditioning plans designed with input from each team's coaching staff. Injury rates during the first month of competitive play dropped noticeably across most teams, with the most significant declines seen in sports involving repetitive high-impact movements, such as basketball and volleyball.
options: Injury rates increased most in sports with repetitive high-impact movements.
Every sport showed an identical reduction in injury rates.
The type of conditioning program had no bearing on injury rates in any sport.
Sport-specific conditioning appears to have most benefited sports with repetitive high-impact movements.
quests.correctAnswer: Sport-specific conditioning appears to have most benefited sports with repetitive high-impact movements.
quests.hint: Notice which specific sports showed the largest change in injury rates.
quests.explanation: Injury rates dropped across most teams but declined most sharply in high-impact sports like basketball and volleyball, suggesting the sport-specific approach was especially valuable for sports with more repetitive physical strain.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional arts council that distributes grant funding to local theater companies began requiring applicants to submit a brief video pitch in addition to the standard written proposal. Council members reported that their funding decisions changed for roughly fifteen percent of applications after watching the videos, most often shifting toward smaller, less established companies whose written proposals had not fully conveyed the energy of their planned productions.
options: The video pitches consistently favored larger, more established companies.
Funding decisions were identical whether or not council members watched the videos.
The video pitches appear to have helped smaller companies convey something their written proposals missed.
Smaller companies were less likely to receive funding after the video requirement began.
quests.correctAnswer: The video pitches appear to have helped smaller companies convey something their written proposals missed.
quests.hint: Notice which type of company most often benefited when decisions changed.
quests.explanation: Funding decisions shifted for some applications after videos were added, most often toward smaller companies, suggesting the video format captured something about their planned productions that the written proposals alone hadn't conveyed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large catering company that tracked food waste across dozens of events found that events using a buffet-style service generated significantly more uneaten food per guest than events using a plated, pre-portioned service, even when the total amount of food prepared per guest was calculated to be roughly the same across both service styles, according to the company's kitchen records.
options: Plated service generated more food waste than buffet-style service.
Buffet-style service appears to generate more food waste than plated service.
Both service styles produced identical amounts of food waste.
The amount of food prepared varied significantly between the two service styles.
quests.correctAnswer: Buffet-style service appears to generate more food waste than plated service.
quests.hint: Compare food waste per guest between the two service styles, noting that preparation amounts were similar.
quests.explanation: Buffet-style events produced more uneaten food per guest than plated events, even with similar preparation amounts, suggesting the serving style itself, not the quantity of food made, influenced how much went to waste.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An outdoor gear retailer that had always processed returns only at physical store locations began accepting mail-in returns with a prepaid shipping label included in every online order. Online sales grew significantly in the two quarters following the change, and customer surveys revealed that many first-time online shoppers cited the easier return policy as a primary reason they felt comfortable ordering gear, such as boots, without trying them on first.
options: Online sales declined after the return policy changed.
The easier return policy appears to have encouraged more first-time online purchases.
Customers cited the return policy as a reason to avoid online shopping.
The return policy had no bearing on customers' comfort with online orders.
quests.correctAnswer: The easier return policy appears to have encouraged more first-time online purchases.
quests.hint: Think about what risk a customer takes when buying gear like boots without trying it on.
quests.explanation: Online sales grew and many first-time online shoppers specifically credited the easier return policy, suggesting the policy reduced the risk customers felt about ordering items like boots without trying them on first.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional pharmacy chain that began offering a free medication synchronization service, coordinating refill dates so patients could pick up all their prescriptions in a single monthly visit rather than several separate trips, found that patients enrolled in the program had notably higher rates of taking medications exactly as prescribed, based on refill timing data collected over the following year.
options: Synchronizing refill dates appears to have improved medication adherence among enrolled patients.
Medication adherence declined among patients enrolled in the synchronization program.
The synchronization service had no measurable effect on adherence.
Patients enrolled in the program made more separate pharmacy trips than before.
quests.correctAnswer: Synchronizing refill dates appears to have improved medication adherence among enrolled patients.
quests.hint: Think about how reducing the number of separate pharmacy trips might affect whether patients pick up their medications on time.
quests.explanation: Patients using the synchronization service showed higher medication adherence based on refill timing, suggesting that consolidating trips to a single monthly visit made it easier for patients to stay on track with their prescriptions.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team analyzing usage data for a note-taking app found that users who created their first note within the initial two minutes of opening the app for the very first time were retained at dramatically higher rates after thirty days than users who spent those first two minutes browsing settings, tutorials, or the app's other features without creating any content of their own.
options: Browsing settings and tutorials first led to better long-term retention.
What users did in their first two minutes had no bearing on retention.
Retention rates were identical regardless of initial user behavior.
Creating content immediately during first use appears linked to better long-term retention.
quests.correctAnswer: Creating content immediately during first use appears linked to better long-term retention.
quests.hint: Compare thirty-day retention between users who created a note right away and users who explored the app first.
quests.explanation: Users who created a note within their first two minutes were retained at much higher rates than users who explored other features first, suggesting that experiencing the app's core function early on matters for whether users stick with it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A nonprofit organization that had always conducted annual performance reviews as a single formal meeting once a year switched to brief, informal check-ins held every two weeks between managers and staff. Employee turnover during the following year dropped to its lowest level in the organization's history, and exit interviews with the small number of employees who did leave rarely mentioned communication or feedback as a reason for departing.
options: Turnover reached its highest level after the check-ins were introduced.
Employees who left most often cited a lack of feedback.
Frequent informal check-ins appear connected to lower turnover and fewer feedback-related departures.
The frequency of performance conversations had no bearing on turnover.
quests.correctAnswer: Frequent informal check-ins appear connected to lower turnover and fewer feedback-related departures.
quests.hint: Notice two separate pieces of evidence in the passage: the turnover rate and what departing employees said.
quests.explanation: Turnover dropped to a record low, and departing employees rarely cited communication as a reason for leaving, suggesting the more frequent check-ins addressed feedback concerns that might otherwise have driven people to quit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A researcher studying long-distance grandparent relationships found that grandchildren who had a standing weekly video call with a grandparent, even a brief one, could name significantly more details about that grandparent's childhood and life history in a follow-up interview than grandchildren who saw a distant grandparent only during occasional holiday visits scattered throughout the year, according to interviews conducted when the grandchildren reached their early teenage years.
options: Occasional holiday visits led to grandchildren knowing more family history.
How often grandchildren saw a grandparent had no bearing on what they knew about them.
Regular weekly video calls appear linked to grandchildren retaining more family history.
Grandchildren in both groups recalled an identical amount of family history.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular weekly video calls appear linked to grandchildren retaining more family history.
quests.hint: Compare what grandchildren remembered based on how often they connected with a distant grandparent.
quests.explanation: Grandchildren with standing weekly video calls recalled more about their grandparent's life history than those who only saw a grandparent occasionally, suggesting frequent, if brief, contact helped preserve and pass along family stories.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city public works department that had always mowed roadside grass on a fixed biweekly schedule throughout the growing season switched to a reduced mowing schedule for several designated stretches of road, allowing wildflowers to grow. Beekeepers in the area reported healthier hive activity near the unmowed stretches, while the department itself reported meaningful savings in fuel and labor costs over the course of the season.
options: Reduced mowing harmed both pollinator activity and the department's budget.
Fuel and labor costs increased under the reduced mowing schedule.
Beekeepers reported no change in hive activity near the unmowed areas.
Reduced mowing appears to have benefited both local pollinators and the department's budget.
quests.correctAnswer: Reduced mowing appears to have benefited both local pollinators and the department's budget.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate positive outcomes of the reduced mowing schedule.
quests.explanation: Beekeepers observed healthier hive activity and the department saved on fuel and labor after reducing mowing, suggesting the change benefited both the local ecosystem and the city's budget at the same time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A community college that had always required all incoming students to take a placement test before enrolling in math courses began instead using high school transcript data to place a portion of students directly into college-level courses. Students placed using transcript data passed their first college math course at rates comparable to students who had taken the placement test, but completed their overall math requirement roughly one semester faster on average.
options: Students placed using transcripts failed their first course far more often.
Transcript-based placement slowed down how quickly students completed their math requirement.
Transcript-based placement appears to help students complete math requirements faster without harming pass rates.
Pass rates and completion speed were both unaffected by the placement method.
quests.correctAnswer: Transcript-based placement appears to help students complete math requirements faster without harming pass rates.
quests.hint: Notice the passage compares two outcomes: pass rates and how quickly students finished their requirement.
quests.explanation: Pass rates stayed similar between the two placement methods, but students placed by transcript finished their math requirement faster, suggesting the traditional placement test may have been placing some capable students into courses below their actual level.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A streaming platform that recommends content based primarily on what similar users have watched noticed that when it added a secondary recommendation row based specifically on genres a user had rated highly in the past, regardless of what other users watched, time spent browsing before selecting something to watch dropped noticeably, particularly among users who had been active on the platform for more than a year.
options: Browsing time increased after the genre-based row was added.
The genre-based recommendation row appears to have helped experienced users choose content more quickly.
The new recommendation row had no measurable effect on browsing time.
New users benefited the most from the genre-based recommendation row.
quests.correctAnswer: The genre-based recommendation row appears to have helped experienced users choose content more quickly.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of users showed the biggest change in browsing time.
quests.explanation: Browsing time dropped after the genre-based row was added, especially among users active for more than a year, suggesting that recommendations based on personal taste, not just similar users, helped experienced users decide faster.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional bus company that had always required exact cash fare, causing frequent delays as drivers made change or resolved disputes, switched entirely to a tap-to-pay card system with no cash option at all. Average boarding time per passenger dropped significantly, and on-time arrival rates for the company's busiest routes improved for the first time in several years, according to internal performance data reviewed by company managers.
options: The switch to tap-to-pay appears to have improved boarding speed and route punctuality.
Boarding time increased after the switch to tap-to-pay.
On-time arrival rates declined for the company's busiest routes.
The payment method had no bearing on boarding time or punctuality.
quests.correctAnswer: The switch to tap-to-pay appears to have improved boarding speed and route punctuality.
quests.hint: Compare boarding time and on-time performance before and after the payment system changed.
quests.explanation: Boarding time dropped and on-time arrivals improved after cash fares were eliminated, suggesting that resolving payment at the door, rather than during boarding, was a meaningful source of the previous delays.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city that had long struggled to fill volunteer positions on its various neighborhood advisory boards began offering a small stipend to cover transportation and childcare costs for meeting attendance, rather than treating the roles as entirely unpaid. Applications for open board seats increased substantially in the following year, with the largest increase coming from residents in lower-income neighborhoods that had previously been underrepresented on the boards.
options: Applications from lower-income neighborhoods decreased after the stipend was introduced.
The stipend appears to have specifically increased participation among lower-income residents.
The stipend had no measurable effect on board applications.
Applications increased equally across every income level in the city.
quests.correctAnswer: The stipend appears to have specifically increased participation among lower-income residents.
quests.hint: Notice which group of residents showed the largest increase in applications.
quests.explanation: Applications rose most sharply among lower-income residents after the stipend was introduced, suggesting that transportation and childcare costs had specifically been keeping that group from volunteering before.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A youth basketball association compared referee retention between two groups: new referees who were paired with an experienced mentor referee for their first ten games, and new referees who officiated those same first ten games independently. Referees who had a mentor were substantially more likely to still be officiating games one full year later than those who started out on their own without any additional guidance from the association.
options: Referees without a mentor were more likely to continue officiating.
Mentorship for new referees appears to improve their likelihood of continuing to officiate long-term.
Mentorship had no bearing on how long new referees continued officiating.
Both groups of referees continued officiating at identical rates.
quests.correctAnswer: Mentorship for new referees appears to improve their likelihood of continuing to officiate long-term.
quests.hint: Compare one-year retention between referees who had a mentor and those who didn't.
quests.explanation: New referees paired with a mentor were more likely to still be officiating a year later than those who started independently, suggesting early mentorship helped new referees stay involved in officiating long-term.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional bank that had always required a minimum balance to avoid a monthly checking account fee eliminated the fee entirely for account holders under age twenty-five. Account openings among that age group rose sharply in the following year, and bank data showed that a meaningful share of those new young account holders also opened a savings account within their first six months, something the bank had not specifically encouraged.
options: Eliminating the fee for young account holders appears to have led to broader engagement with the bank.
Account openings among young people declined after the fee was eliminated.
Young account holders were less likely to open additional accounts.
The fee elimination had no measurable effect on account openings.
quests.correctAnswer: Eliminating the fee for young account holders appears to have led to broader engagement with the bank.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate positive outcomes among young account holders.
quests.explanation: Account openings rose among young people, and many of them also opened savings accounts without being specifically encouraged to, suggesting the fee elimination led to broader engagement with the bank beyond just the checking account itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large school district that switched its cafeteria supplier to one sourcing produce from farms within a hundred miles of its schools found that produce waste actually increased slightly in the first few months, which nutrition staff attributed to unfamiliar fruits and vegetables that students were less accustomed to eating, though staff also noted that overall student satisfaction with cafeteria food, measured by survey, improved during the same period.
options: The switch to local produce appears to have improved satisfaction even though it temporarily increased waste.
The switch reduced both produce waste and student satisfaction.
Student satisfaction with cafeteria food declined after the switch.
Produce waste and student satisfaction were both unaffected by the supplier change.
quests.correctAnswer: The switch to local produce appears to have improved satisfaction even though it temporarily increased waste.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes two different outcomes moving in different directions.
quests.explanation: Waste rose slightly due to unfamiliar produce, but student satisfaction with cafeteria food improved during the same period, suggesting the switch had mixed but not purely negative effects, with satisfaction improving despite the waste increase.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city library system that digitized its collection of local oral histories, recordings of longtime residents describing the neighborhood's past, and made them searchable by keyword online, reported that requests for related printed materials, such as old newspaper clippings and photographs held in its physical archive, increased substantially after the recordings went online, rather than replacing interest in the physical materials as some staff had initially expected.
options: Interest in the physical archive declined after the recordings went online.
The digitized recordings appear to have increased, rather than replaced, interest in the physical archive.
The digitized recordings had no effect on requests for physical materials.
Staff had correctly predicted that digital access would replace interest in physical materials.
quests.correctAnswer: The digitized recordings appear to have increased, rather than replaced, interest in the physical archive.
quests.hint: Notice what staff expected to happen, and compare it with what the passage says actually happened.
quests.explanation: Requests for physical archive materials increased after the oral histories went online, contrary to staff expectations that digital access would reduce interest, suggesting the online recordings sparked curiosity that led people back to the physical collection.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying how people interact with voice assistants found that users who initially set up the device using a scripted, guided tutorial asked significantly more complex, multi-step questions within their first month than users who set up the device by skipping the tutorial and exploring its capabilities entirely on their own through trial and error, based on usage logs the team reviewed across several thousand households.
options: Skipping the tutorial led to more complex questions being asked.
Completing the guided tutorial appears linked to using the device's more advanced capabilities.
How users set up the device had no bearing on the complexity of questions they asked.
Both groups of users asked equally complex questions.
quests.correctAnswer: Completing the guided tutorial appears linked to using the device's more advanced capabilities.
quests.hint: Compare the complexity of questions asked by each group of users.
quests.explanation: Users who completed the guided tutorial asked more complex questions than those who explored on their own, suggesting the tutorial helped users understand the device's fuller range of capabilities from the start.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional health insurer that began covering the full cost of an annual preventive wellness visit, with no copay or deductible required, found that enrollment in the visits rose substantially among members who had not seen a primary care doctor in more than two years, a group the insurer had specifically hoped to reach with the policy change, according to a report the insurer released the following year.
options: Removing the cost barrier appears to have reached the specific group the insurer had targeted.
Members who had recently seen a doctor showed the biggest increase in visits.
The policy change had no measurable effect on wellness visit enrollment.
Enrollment declined among members who had not seen a doctor recently.
quests.correctAnswer: Removing the cost barrier appears to have reached the specific group the insurer had targeted.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of members the passage says showed the biggest change.
quests.explanation: Enrollment rose substantially among members who hadn't seen a doctor in over two years, exactly the group the insurer hoped to reach, suggesting the removal of cost barriers succeeded at its intended goal.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A design agency that had always required employees to submit expense reports through a lengthy internal form found that switching to a simple photo-based app, where employees just photographed a receipt and typed one line of description, reduced the average number of days between a purchase and its reimbursement from three weeks to under five days, according to finance department records reviewed at year's end.
options: Reimbursement times increased after the photo-based app was introduced.
The new app had no measurable effect on reimbursement speed.
The photo-based expense app appears to have significantly sped up employee reimbursements.
Employees stopped submitting expense reports after the app was introduced.
quests.correctAnswer: The photo-based expense app appears to have significantly sped up employee reimbursements.
quests.hint: Compare reimbursement times before and after the expense reporting method changed.
quests.explanation: Reimbursement time dropped from three weeks to under five days after the simpler photo-based app was introduced, suggesting the lengthy internal form had been the main source of delay in the previous process.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since he began preparing all five weekday lunches on Sunday afternoon and storing them in labeled containers, Malik says he no longer buys lunch from the cafe near his office, a habit that used to cost him close to fifteen dollars a day, and he has also noticed he throws away far less unused produce than when he shopped for each meal separately throughout the week.
options: Malik's spending on lunch increased after he began meal prepping.
Malik began throwing away more unused produce after meal prepping.
Meal prepping affected Malik's spending but had no effect on his food waste.
Preparing lunches in advance appears to have reduced both Malik's spending and his food waste.
quests.correctAnswer: Preparing lunches in advance appears to have reduced both Malik's spending and his food waste.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate benefits of Malik's new habit.
quests.explanation: Malik stopped buying expensive cafe lunches and now wastes less produce since he started meal prepping on Sundays, showing the new habit benefited him both financially and in terms of reducing food waste.
